context: A bank savings account pays simple interest at a whole-number percentage per annum. The amount wanted after a whole number of years is given in rand, and the amount to invest now is asked for.
stem: A bank offers a savings account which pays simple interest at a rate of ${=r}$ % per annum. If you want to accumulate $\text{R{=A}}$ in ${=n}$ years, how much should you invest now?
solution: Read the question carefully and write down the given information: $\begin{aligned}A&=\text{R{=A}}\\P&=?\\i&=\frac{{=r}}{100}=0.0{=r}\\n&={=n}\end{aligned}$
Write down the simple interest formula: $A=P(1+in)$
Substitute the given values and work out the bracket: $\begin{aligned}\text{R{=A}}&=P\left(1+0.0{=r}\times{=n}\right)\\\text{R{=A}}&=P\times{=ds}\end{aligned}$
Divide both sides by ${=ds}$ to find $P$: $\begin{aligned}P&=\frac{\text{R{=A}}}{{=ds}}\\&=\text{R{=P}}\end{aligned}$
notes: Entry point of the skill: same skeleton as the book's ex9-1-6 (A = P(1 + in), then divide), but the numbers are built backwards from P = 100m so that A is a whole number of rand and the principal is an exact whole number, with no rounding step. Rate is a single-digit whole percent so i prints as 0.0r. The denominator 1 + in is printed the book's way with trailing zeros dropped (1.3, not 1.30). Numeric family, so no distractors and no misconception ids are needed; none are catalogued for this objective.
